source_text: quae illos illicita commisisse indignatur, hos etiam licita contempsisse miratur; ultimi limitis sortita regionem, ultra se proruentium exsecrata barbariem, supra se micantium venerata fulgorem, quae verecundis manibus et confovet aestuantes, et laudat tali remedio non egentes
pass_a_gloss: Which those illicita commisisse indignatur, these also licita contempsisse miratur; ultimi limitis sortita regionem, ultra himself proruentium exsecrata barbariem, above himself micantium venerata fulgorem, which verecundis manibus and confovet aestuantes, and laudat tali remedio not egentes.
pass_b_english: [Marital chastity] is indignant that some have committed what is forbidden, and marvels that others have renounced even what is permitted. Assigned the territory at the furthest boundary, it condemns the savagery of those who rush beyond it and reveres the radiance of those who shine above it. With modest hands it both tends those burning with desire and praises those who do not need such a remedy.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
